thread:
Emma: Heads-up — saw a p99 jump on the small-llm prod fleet after yesterday's kernel-selector rollout. p50 ~ same, p95 +10ms, p99 +120ms. Repro on canary.

Raj: ugh. Any correlation with KV cache miss rate? last night we changed the microbatch timeout heuristic, might be making more partial batches.

Matt: I pulled a short trace. KV miss rate spiked from 4% -> 14% for that workload. Flamegraph shows GPU stall waiting on device->host memcpy around kvmiss path.

Sophie: that matches the kernel A vs kernel B tradeoff we've seen: kernel-A (optimized for dense perf) gives better tokens/sec but is sensitive to kvmiss and causes longer tail because it relies on host fallback path. Kernel-B trades a bit of throughput for more consistent tail.

Emma: repro notes (short):
```
# canary run
git rev: perf/regress/kv-prefetch-2026-03-17
batching.conf: {"microbatch_size": 8, "max_batch_time_ms": 6, "continuous_batching": true}
workload: small-llm-short-context, 1k qps traffic replay
```
Observed timeline: kernel-selector picked kernel-A 98% of calls, p99 jumps inside 30s of warmup.

Raj: why did selector prefer kernel-A? selector uses latency-first when expected_seq < 256 and throughput-first when >256. This workload has mostly short seqs but our recent kernel-performance table updated A as faster median, so selector switched.

Matt: I ran a quick microbatch sweep locally: microbatch_size=1/2/4/8. Results (tokens/sec / p99):
- 1 -> 520 t/s / 160ms p99
- 2 -> 880 t/s / 180ms p99
- 4 -> 1200 t/s / 210ms p99
- 8 -> 1600 t/s / 340ms p99
So larger microbatches increase throughput but amplify p99 when KV miss rate is non-trivial.

Sophie: this is the classic headroom vs saturation trade. If we push for 80-90% GPU util we get cost wins but tails blow up under kvmiss spikes. For a 99 SLO we might need to target lower util or stronger admission.

Emma: proposal: revert selector decision on canary to prefer kernel-B for short sequences (force kernel-policy=stable-tail), AND temporarily change admission target util from 85% -> 70% for that pool. Also add a kvcache warmup probe during load ramp to cut miss tail.

Raj: alternative: keep kernel-A for throughput, but apply microbatch cap for requests with recent KV miss history and route them to kernel-B, or fast-fail a tiny subset to reduce tail amplification (soft-shed). Could add a per-req flag if kv_lookup_time > X to avoid batching.

Matt: experiment plan: run A/B with 10% traffic on canary for 4h each:
- A: selector=kernel-B, microbatch_max=4, admission_target=70%
- B: selector=kernel-A, microbatch_max=2, admission_target=85%, kv_prefetch=true
Measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec and GPU stall percentage.

ci-bot: deploy scheduled -> canary pool (3 nodes) at 2026-03-17T14:10Z. Rollout steps: canary -> stable if p99 delta < 15ms and error rate < 0.05%.

Sophie: small perf-regression root cause hypothesis: recent kernel-A lib changed memcpy ordering for KV fallback which serializes device activity more. We should run a microtrace capturing memcpy timings and kernel launch latencies.

Emma: action items:
- Emma: run the A/B canary and collect perf traces (2h each)
- Raj: add lightweight kvcache-warmup probe and a metric for per-request kv_miss_latency
- Matt: add a flamegraph capture around host<->device memcpy and post results in this thread
- Sophie: prepare rollback patch for kernel-selector and microbatch cap if canary fails

Raj: quick note — if we add prefetch we should tighten the admission controller to prefer headroom at the start of burst (grace period 30s) so prefetch can warm KV.

Emma: agree. I'll kick off the runs now and dump logs to //s3/perf/2187659999/. Will post results in ~3h. Thanks :thumbsup:

Matt: thanks. if anyone sees a spike in errors while I'm running local sims say now so I can stop.

Sophie: pinged infra to expand canary quota if needed.

ci-bot: canary deploy started (job id: canary-2187659999-1).
